parent_ahobilam_faq_0_d4a596:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Who is the presiding deity of Ahobilam?
Answer: Lord Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy is the presiding deity, manifested in nine forms (Nava Narasimha) across the Garudadri hills.
parent_ahobilam_faq_1_9b8169:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the timings of Lower and Upper Ahobilam?
Answer: Lower temple is open from 6:30 AM – 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM – 8:00 PM. Upper temple is open from 7:00 AM – 1:00 PM and 2:00 PM – 5:30 PM.
parent_ahobilam_faq_2_3559a4:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Can we book rooms or sevas online?
Answer: No. Room reservations and seva tickets must be booked at the counters or by contacting the Malola Guest House office.
parent_ahobilam_faq_3_9ba710:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: How difficult is the trek to Upper Ahobilam?
Answer: Treks range from easy (Karanja Narasimha) to highly strenuous (Jwala Narasimha and Ugra Sthambham), which involve steep climbing and river beds.
parent_ahobilam_faq_4_0e659a:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the Doli charges for elderly people?
Answer: Doli services are available at Lower Ahobilam for the steep climb. Rates vary depending on the trek destination and should be verified locally.
parent_ahobilam_faq_5_c3b491:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What is the significance of the Swathi Nakshatram?
Answer: Swathi Nakshatram is the birth star of Lord Narasimha, during which grand Thirumanjanam (Abhishekam) is performed for all nine Narasimha deities.
parent_ahobilam_faq_6_05a4d1:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is there free food (Annadanam) available?
Answer: Yes. The Annamacharya Nitya Annadanam Trust provides free meals to all devotees three times daily.
parent_ahobilam_faq_7_e5094c:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: How can we reach Ahobilam?
Answer: Ahobilam is ~30 km from Allagadda town. Buses ply from Allagadda every 45 minutes. Taxis can be hired from Nandyal or Kadapa railway stations.
parent_ahobilam_faq_8_d88a2b:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is there any dress code for Darshan?
Answer: Yes. Modest traditional attire is expected. Shorts, lungis, and sleeveless clothing are prohibited.
parent_ahobilam_faq_9_780dc9:

Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Are there any forest restrictions for travelers?
Answer: Yes. Devotees are not allowed to stay or trek in Upper Ahobilam after sunset as it is in a tiger reserve forest zone.
parent_ahobilam_festivals_complete:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Festivals
File: festivals.json

Festival Name: Annual Brahmotsavams (Masi Mahotsavam)
Description: The annual Brahmotsavam is celebrated in the month of Masi (mid-February to mid-March) lasting for 10 days. The processional deity Lord Prahlada Varadhan is taken out in colorful Vahanas. It is a major notified festival attracting lakhs of devotees. A key ritual is the distribution of the highly sacred "Garuda Prasadam", sought by childless couples.
Month: Masi (mid-February to mid-March)
Importance: Major notified festival attracting lakhs of devotees. Features processional deity Lord Prahlada Varadhan on colorful Vahanas and distribution of the highly sacred Garuda Prasadam.

---

Festival Name: Monthly Swathi Nakshatram
Description: Swathi Nakshatram is the birth star of Lord Narasimha. Every month on this day, special mass Abhishekam (Thirumanjanam) is performed for all the nine Narasimha deities across the hills. Devotees travel from Chennai, Bangalore, and Hyderabad to sponsor or witness this holy bathing ceremony.
Month: Monthly (Swathi Nakshatram)
Importance: Birth star of Lord Narasimha. Mass bathing ceremony (Abhishekam/Thirumanjanam) for all nine Narasimha deities.

---

Festival Name: Narasimha Jayanthi
Description: Narasimha Jayanthi is celebrated annually in May (Vaisakha month) with special rituals, night-long prayers, and massive food distribution schemes (Tadiyaradhanam).
Month: May (Vaisakha month)
Importance: Annual incarnation day celebrations featuring special rituals, night-long prayers, and massive food distribution (Tadiyaradhanam).

parent_ahobilam_dress_code_8bd0c881:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Dress Code
File: rules.json

Darshan Dress Code: decent traditional Indian outfits.
Women: Sarees or salwar kameez with dupatta.
Men: Dhotis, panchas, or formal shirts and trousers. Lungis, shorts, and sleeveless tops are strictly prohibited.
parent_ahobilam_dos_ae504044:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Dos
File: rules.json

- Do trekking in groups and complete Upper Ahobilam visits well before sunset due to wild animals.
- Do hire a local guide for the strenuous trek to Jwala Narasimha and Ugra Sthambham.
- Do wear sturdy, slip-resistant walking shoes or sandals for trekking (footwear is removed outside individual shrines).
- Do carry sufficient drinking water to prevent dehydration during the mountain climbs.
- Do protect your belongings and prasadams from wild monkeys in the forest paths.
parent_ahobilam_donts_5e3f5364:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Donts
File: rules.json

- Don't litter the forest or Nallamala hill reserve paths with plastics, bottles, or food packets.
- Don't attempt to climb Ugra Sthambham if you suffer from vertigo, high blood pressure, or breathing issues.
- Don't venture off the marked trekking pathways into the deep forest areas.
- Don't take photographs inside the inner cave sanctums of the Narasimha shrines.
- Don't stay overnight in the Upper Ahobilam forest area; all visitors must return to Lower Ahobilam before dark.
parent_ahobilam_forest_restrictions_29b2:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Forest Restrictions
File: rules.json

Forest Restrictions: Ahobilam is in a tiger reserve forest zone. Devotees are not allowed to stay or trek in Upper Ahobilam after sunset.

parent_ahobilam_description_5f1bb270:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Description
File: temple.json

Description: Sri Ahobila Lakshmi Nrisimha Swamy Temple, the abode of Lord Narasimha situated in the Nallamala Hills of Nandyal District in Andhra Pradesh, is a highly ancient and revered Vaishnavite pilgrimage center. The shrine deserves a special mention in terms of its unique geographical layout, dense forest surroundings, and deep spiritual sanctity, being considered a "Svayam Vyakta Kshetram" (self-manifested shrine). The Eastern Ghats are traditionally likened to the great serpent Adisesha, with Ahobilam representing its middle fold, Tirumala the hood, and Srisailam the tail. Ahobilam is divided into two areas: Diguvu Ahobilam (Lower Ahobilam) and Eguvu Ahobilam (Upper Ahobilam), separated by a distance of approximately 12.8 km. Sri Ahobila Muth, one of India's most prominent Sri Vaishnava religious institutions established over 600 years ago, administers the temple.
parent_ahobilam_history_4180d2d4:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: History
File: temple.json

History: Sri Ahobila Muth was established over 600 years ago and administers the temple under hereditary trusteeship. A prominent Jayasthambham (victory pillar) erected in the spacious ground outside the lower temple marks the historical victory of Emperor Krishnadeva Raya of the Vijayanagara Empire. Additional structures were built by Kakatiya kings, especially Pratapa Rudra. Sri Ahobila Muth was founded here by Kidambi Srinivasachar under the instructions of Lord Narasimha, taking the ascetic name Srimad Adivan Satakopan Jeeyar. The portable metal deity (Utsava Moorthy) of the Malola Narasimha temple (meaning "beloved to Lakshmi") is the presiding traveling deity of the pontiffs (Azhagiya Singars) of the Muth, which accompanies them on their spiritual tours across India.
parent_ahobilam_mythology_0901c68f:
Temple: Ahobilam
Category: Mythology
File: temple.json

Mythology: Puranas like the Brahmanda Purana, Koorma Purana, Padma Purana, and Vishnu Purana mention this place as the capital and palace of the demon king Hiranyakasipu. It is here that Sriman Narayana incarnated as the half-man, half-lion Lord Narasimha to slay the demon and protect his child devotee Prahlada. The word "Ahobilam" is derived from two legends: "Aho Balam" (expression of the Gods praising the incredible strength of Lord Narasimha after slaying the demon) or "Aho Bilam" (signifying the great cave where the self-manifested deity was worshipped by Garuda). The Mackenzie Collection's "Ahobilam Kaifiyat" in Telugu contains village register records detailing this legend.

parent_badrachalam_tips_e40cc90e:
Temple: Badrachalam
Category: Tips
File: crowd.json

- Barricaded Queue Compartments: Steel queue corridors regulate devotee traffic, with temporary holding compartments providing drinking water and seating during peak festivals.
- Token Systems: Barcode and physical slot tokens are distributed during large-scale festivals to systematically stagger entry times and control crowd density.
- Darshan Waiting Times: General free Sarva Darshan queues take roughly 1 hour on normal weekdays, scaling up to several hours during core festival seasons.
- Police Deployment: Extensive local police contingents secure the temple parameters, Mithila Stadium grounds, and Godavari bathing ghats during major events.
- Godavari Bathing Arrangements: Certified lifeguards, divers, patrol boats, and safety lifebuoys are deployed at the riverbanks during peak festival seasons.
- Medical Camps: Temporary medical response tents are erected near Mithila Stadium and the riverbanks to manage emergency healthcare and distribute hydration packets.
- Shuttle Services: Private vehicles face restrictions at town boundaries during major festivals, with the state transit corporation running dedicated pilgrim shuttle buses.
- Public Announcement (PA) Systems: High-power PA systems across the shrine complex, stadium, and riverbanks broadcast safety updates and direct foot traffic.
- Special Entry Darshan: Paid speed queue ticket options are available at the counter for ₹50 and ₹100 to bypass standard free lines.
- VIP Break Darshan: Dedicated VIP Break Darshan access is available at a fixed tier of ₹250 per individual during specific management windows.
- Antaralaya Abhishekam: The premium Sunday morning ritual requires a specialized ticket tier priced officially at ₹500.

Festival Name: Vaikuntha Ekadashi (Mukkoti Ekadashi)
Description: Vaikuntha Ekadashi (Mukkoti Ekadashi) is observed on Sunday, 20 December 2026.
Teppotsavam (Float Festival): Celebrated on Dashami evening (19 December 2026). The deities are taken in a colorful procession on a swan-shaped boat (Hamsa Vahanam) in the Godavari River, accompanied by fireworks.
Uttara Dwara Darshanam: Opens at dawn (around 5:00 AM) on Ekadashi morning (20 December 2026). Devotees enter through the Northern Gate, representing entry into Vaikuntha.
Mukkoti Dwadashi Dwara Darshanam: Observed on the following day with special offerings and distribution of holy prasadam.
Month: Margashirsha Masam
Importance: Major festival where pilgrims enter through Uttara Dwara (Northern Gate) representing entry into Vaikuntha, preceded by Teppotsavam on Dashami evening and followed by Mukkoti Dwadashi Dwara Darshanam.

Month: Pushya Masam (January)
Importance: Musical and devotional festival honoring Bhakta Ramadasu with Gosthi Gana Sankeerthana of his Navaratna Keerthanas.

Medical Emergencies: Report immediately to the first aid clinic near the administrative block. For transfer to Government Area Hospital, dial 108.
Godavari River Bathing Safety: Always stay within the protective steel fencing. Do not venture into deep waters; currents are strong and unpredictable. Children must be supervised at all times.
Flood Season Monsoon: If Godavari levels exceed the warning levels (First Warning: 43 feet, Second Warning: 48 feet, Third Warning: 53 feet), river bathing is suspended. Follow instructions given via public address systems.
Heat Precautions During Summer: Temperatures in Bhadrachalam can exceed 40°C in summer (April–June). Devotees are advised to stay hydrated, and the temple administration lays carpet/mats along the walkways.

Description: The Sree Seetha Ramachandra Swamy Devasthanam at Bhadrachalam, situated on the banks of the River Godavari in the Bhadradri Kothagudem district of Telangana, is revered as a premier Vaishnavite shrine in India. Popularly known as "Dakshina Ayodhya" (Southern Ayodhya), it is a historic center of Rama-worship, spiritual Carnatic music, and ancient Vedic traditions.

Vaikunta Chaturbhuja Rama (Unique Deity Form):
Bhadrachalam is globally unique because Lord Rama is worshipped here in the form of Vaikunta Rama or Chaturbhuja Rama (four-armed Rama). Unlike standard representations where Lord Rama has two arms holding a bow and arrow, the Swayambhu deity here holds a bow (Dhanus) and arrow in two hands, and Shankha (conch) and Chakra (discus) in the other two—emblems of Lord Vishnu. Goddess Seetha Devi is seated on His left lap, and His brother Lakshmana stands to His right. This represents the Lord in His transcendent Vaikunta state while simultaneously maintaining His mortal incarnation as Rama.

The Holy Godavari River:
A profound spiritual feature of Bhadrachalam is the Godavari River, which flows as "Dakshina Vahini" (southward flow) at this specific location. Taking a holy dip in the Godavari, especially during Pushkarams or auspicious Hindu months, is believed to cleanse sins and bestow divine merit.
parent_badrachalam_history_f66089a6:
Temple: Badrachalam
Category: History
File: temple.json

History: Pokala Dhammakka: A tribal woman who had a dream where Lord Rama revealed the location of the Swayambhu idols hidden inside an anthill. She cleared the anthill using Godavari water and began performing basic daily bhajan and worship in a simple thatched structure.

Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna): A 17th-century Tehsildar of Bhadrachalam under the Qutb Shahi dynasty. He utilized six lakh rupees of government revenue to construct the grand stone temple. Consequently, he was imprisoned in Golconda Fort for 12 years by Sultan Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tanishah). While in prison, he composed the immortal Ramadasu Keertanalu (devotional Carnatic songs). According to historical faith, Lord Rama and Lakshmana disguised themselves as royal servants (Ramoji and Laxmoji) and repaid the Sultan six lakh gold coins (Ramatankas) to secure Ramadasu's release.
parent_badrachalam_mythology_b7b6624d:
Temple: Badrachalam
Category: Mythology
File: temple.json

Mythology: According to the Skanda Purana, the hillock upon which the temple stands is named after Bhadra Maharshi, the son of Mount Meru and Menaka. Bhadra Maharshi performed intense penance on the banks of the Godavari to receive the blessings of Lord Rama. Pleased with his devotion, Lord Vishnu manifested in His Vaikunta Rama form. Fulfilling the sage's wish, the Lord permanently resided on the hill, turning Bhadra Maharshi's body into the hillock (Bhadrachalam) that supports the temple.

parent_badrachalam_architecture_01298540:
Temple: Badrachalam

Style: Blend of Dravidian styles, built primarily during the 17th century by Bhakta Ramadasu, incorporating features from the Vijayanagara and Chola traditions.

Highlights:
    Name: The Rajagopuram
    Description: Reaching towards the sky, the main gopuram faces the Godavari River, acting as the main gateway to the temple. Its tiers are adorned with elaborate carvings depicting scenes from the Ramayana.
---
    Name: Inner Sanctum (Garbhalayam)
    Description: The sanctum sanctorum houses the self-manifested icons of Vaikunta Rama (four-armed, seated in padmasana), Seetha Devi (seated on His left lap), and Lakshmana (standing to His right).
---
    Name: The Sudarsana Chakra
    Description: A golden Sudarsana Chakra sits at the crest of the temple's main Vimana tower. Legend states that Bhakta Ramadasu retrieved this sacred eight-faced disc from the Godavari River following a dream instruction from Lord Rama.
---
    Name: Ramadasu Dhyana Mandiram
    Description: A dedicated meditation hall inside the temple complex that showcases the life of Kancharla Gopanna, including representations of the historical Ramatanka gold coins.
---
    Name: Mithila Stadium (Kalyana Mandapam)
    Description: A large open-air pavilion located near the temple, specifically designed to accommodate devotees during the annual Sri Rama Navami Kalyanotsavam.
---

parent_balkampet_description_2009041b:
Temple: Balkampet
Category: Description
File: temple.json

Description: The Sri Yellamma Pochamma Devasthanam (Balkampet Yellamma Temple) is a historic Hindu shrine located in Balkampet, Hyderabad, Telangana. The temple is famous for its unique physical layout, wherein the main self-manifested (Swayambhu) idol of the Goddess is situated approximately 10 feet below ground level and is partially submerged in water, giving her the name Jala Durga. It is a major spiritual center in Hyderabad, drawing crowds on Sundays and Tuesdays, and is famous for the annual Bonalu Jathara and Yellamma Kalyanotsavam festivals. A historic well is located in the temple complex, and the water is called Theertham. Devotees believe that the water in the well is a cure to all ailments, and a bath/sprinkling of this water purifies skin diseases. Devotees offer animal sacrifices in the form of chickens and goats (traditionally performed in surrounding areas). Managed by the Endowments Department of the Government of Telangana under the supervision of an Executive Officer (EO). Temple Type: Hindu Goddess Temple (Shakta Tradition). Primary Source: Official Temple Website.
parent_balkampet_history_446da28a:
Temple: Balkampet
Category: History
File: temple.json

History: The temple devasthanam was first constructed in the 15th Century AD. The idol of the Goddess is located 10 feet deeper than the ground level. The temple took its current form later, during renovations in the early 20th Century AD. An Akhand Jyoth (eternal lamp) was lit during the renovation and remains burning in the temple. Primary Source: Official Temple Website, About Us Page (https://balkampettemple.telangana.gov.in/about_us/) under the "About Us" section.
parent_balkampet_mythology_123ddbee:
Temple: Balkampet
Category: Mythology
File: temple.json

Mythology: The primary legend associated with the temple is the traditional story of Renuka Devi:
• The Story of Renuka: Renuka, daughter of Raja Renuka, was married to sage Jamadagni (son of Satyavati). They had five sons, including Parashurama. One day, Renuka failed to perform one of her regular household duties, which angered Jamadagni. He banished her, and she was advised by saints to perform penance by doing pujas in front of a Shivalinga and feed Brahmins.
• The Execution: Jamadagni, still furious, commanded his sons to punish their mother. The four eldest refused and were burned to ashes by their father's gaze. The youngest son, Parashurama, obeyed his father and set out with an axe. He found his mother hiding in a village and beheaded her, along with the village woman who had been hiding her.
• The Resurrection Mismatch: Jamadagni, pleased with Parashurama's obedience, granted him a boon. Parashurama asked for the lives of his mother, brothers, and the village woman to be restored. During the process of joining the heads back to the bodies, the head of Renuka was mistakenly restored to the village woman's body, and vice versa. Jamadagni accepted the form with Renuka's body, and the other form (village woman's body with Renuka's head) became known as Yellamma (mother of all).
• Kali Incarnation: Goddess Yellamma is also believed to be an incarnation of Goddess Kali, explaining the celebratory nature of the Bonalu festival.

- General Rules: Keep in mind that mobile phones are restricted inside the main complex.

- Warn readers that if heavy floods occur, step access to the bathing ghat may be temporarily closed by the district administration for safety.
- Crucial Temple Redevelopment Notice: The primary temple structure is currently undergoing a massive ₹225 crore transformation. Because of this, all main rituals, darshans, and Aksharabhyasam sevas have been systematically moved to a temporary, downsized structure called the Bala Alayam. Question: What are the main operating timings of the Basara Temple?
Answer: The temple opens daily at 4:00 AM and closes at 8:30 PM. There is a mandatory afternoon break when the sanctum doors close from 12:30 PM to 2:00 PM.
parent_basara_faq_1_1cbc98:
Temple: Basara
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is there a strict dress code for devotees visiting the temple?
Answer: Yes. Devotees must wear traditional Indian or modest clothing. Men should wear traditional dhotis, panchas, or kurtas with pyjamas. Women are required to wear sarees or traditional chudidars with dupattas. Modern Western attire like shorts, sleeveless tops, or short skirts is strictly prohibited at the entrance gates.
parent_basara_faq_2_f74298:
Temple: Basara
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Are there any unique code-of-conduct rules pilgrims must follow?
Answer: Yes. While you are fully allowed to carry flowers as an offering to Goddess Saraswathi, pilgrims are strictly forbidden from wearing flower garlands or pinning decorative loose flowers in their hair when entering the temple boundaries.
parent_basara_faq_3_333da2:
Temple: Basara
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the official timings for the Aksharabhyasam ceremony?
Answer: The educational initiation ritual is performed across two main operational batches daily: a Morning Session from 7:30 AM to 12:00 PM and an Afternoon Session from 2:00 PM to 6:00 PM.
parent_basara_faq_4_b2ed21:
Temple: Basara
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What materials do parents need to bring for the ceremony?
Answer: The official ticket package covers the essential ritual elements. However, parents should carry a writing slate (palaka), chalk pencils, and a small notebook. Note that outside rice grains or raw tracing trays are not allowed; the temple provides the ritual rice-tracing plates internally.
parent_basara_faq_5_2edb17:
Temple: Basara
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: When does the temple experience the highest crowd volumes?
Answer: Peak traffic occurs during Vasant Panchami (January/February), which draws 40,000 to 50,000+ daily visitors. The 10-day Dasara Navaratri festival and Maha Shivaratri also experience significant surges, with daily counts reaching 25,000 pilgrims.
parent_basara_faq_6_14ab60:
Temple: Basara
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: How long is the wait time for Darshan on festival days?
Answer: On standard weekdays, general darshan takes roughly 30 to 45 minutes. During major seasonal festivals, expect a baseline queue wait time of 2 to 3 hours, along with an additional 1 to 2 hours if you are concurrently joining the Aksharabhyasam lanes.
parent_basara_faq_7_5b28c8:
Temple: Basara
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is the nearby Godavari River safe for bathing and boating year-round?
Answer: No, conditions depend strictly on the season. During the Monsoon (July to October), the rain-fed river experiences strong, deep currents where bathing is restricted for safety. During Summer (March to June), the water levels recede significantly, halting boating entirely. The safest and most stable time for a holy dip is Winter (November to February).

parent_basara_dos_fb55b935:
Temple: Basara
Category: Dos
File: rules.json

- Do pay obeisance to your Ishta Divam or Kula Divam before you start for Basara.
- Do bathe in the Godavari and worship Sri Gnana Saraswathi Devi.
- Do bathe and wear clean clothes (wear a dhoti with upper cloth) before you enter the temple.
- Do concentrate only on Sri Gnana Saraswathi Devi inside the temple.
- Do observe absolute silence inside the temple and chant "Om Sri Saraswathyei namo namaha" to yourself.
- Do respect ancient customs while in Basara.
- Do pay obeisance (Pranaamam) with two hands. "Mukulitha Hastha Pranaamam" is auspecious.
- Do respect and Promote religious sentiments among the co-pilgrims.
- Do deposit your offerings in the Hundi.
- Do wear a tilakadharana in accordance with Hindu religion.
- One who regards his Guru (preceptor) as a mere human being, the lords Bimba as only a stone image, the Vedic mantras as just a means of livelihood and one who is indifferent to the worship rituals become blameworthy and his would be of no value (nishphalam).
- Be clean physically and mentally.
- Follow the procedures and wait for your turn for the Darshanam of the si Gnana Saraswathi Devi.
- Do respect ladies and be kind towards children and the senior citizens
parent_basara_donts_eac0cadd:
Temple: Basara
Category: Donts
File: rules.json

- Do not carry too much jewelry or cash with you.
- Do not come to Basara for any purpose other than worshipping the Godess.
- Do not eat non-vegetarian food.
- Don't wear footwear or move around in a vehicle, in and around the premises of the temple.
- Don't rush in for Darshanam. But along with the queue.
- Don't prostrate (sastanga danda pranamam) inside the temple. (up to Dhwajasthamba)
- Don't throw away the Prasadam and theertham.
- Don't wear flowers and garlands in Basara; all the flowers are for the Godess only.
- Don't encourage beggars, but do contribute to the needy.
- Don't spit or be a nuisance inside and premises of the temple.
- Don't enter the shrine naked or wearing a piece of lion cloth (Kaupina).
- Don't wear any head guards (helmet, caps, turban, hat etc unless required by your religion.) while entering the temple.
- Don't carry any weapon while entering the temple.
- Don't eat food brought from outside or chew betel leaves while entering the temple or in the temple premises.
- One should not loiter, litter,spit and urinate or defecate around the premises of the temple.
- One should not have gossip or talk about sexuality while in the temple.
- Having entered a temple , one should never commit an act of violence, harshness in the premises.
- Standing in god's presence one must never utter a lie.
- One should not quarrel in a temple on any account, the temple is not a place for it.
- One should not talk about his wealth, money, status and Ahamkara but be obedient to God in the temple.
- One should not bow before another person while in a temple; God is the only Lord for all.
- One should not sit with his back to the deity in the temple.
- There are sequences of poojas ans sevas in the temple and one should have patience to have the darshanam of the Lord.
- Making pranamam (obeisance) with only one hand to the Godess is prohibited. Use both hands.

All daily darshans, poojas, and Akshara Abhyasam (child learning initiation ceremonies) are operating normally from this temporary structure, but visitors should expect a smaller prayer area.Crucial Temple Redevelopment Notice: The primary temple structure is currently undergoing a massive ₹225 crore transformation. parent_birla_mandir_faq_0_36764e:
Temple: Birla Mandir
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What makes the Birla Temple in Hyderabad architecturally unique?
Answer: The temple is constructed entirely out of 2,000 tonnes of pure white marble brought from Rajasthan. It stands atop the 280-foot-high Naubath Pahad hillock and beautifully blends three distinct architectural styles: Dravidian, Rajasthani, and Utkala (Odisha).
parent_birla_mandir_faq_1_9db6b7:
Temple: Birla Mandir
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Who built the temple and when was it opened to the public?
Answer: The temple was commissioned by the visionary industrialist and philanthropist Dr. B.D. Birla. Skilled artisans laboured for over 10 years to complete the monument, and it was opened to the public in 1976 under the care of the Birla Group of Industries.
parent_birla_mandir_faq_2_4abd24:
Temple: Birla Mandir
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Which deity is worshipped as the main idol inside the temple?
Answer: The temple is dedicated to Lord Venkateshwara (an incarnation of Lord Vishnu). The inner sanctum houses a magnificent 11-foot-tall statue of the deity sculpted meticulously out of dark granite stone.
parent_birla_mandir_faq_3_afd73f:
Temple: Birla Mandir
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Category: Timings, Entry, & Rules FAQs
Question: What are the daily operating hours for visitors?
Answer: The temple follows strict split timings every day:
Morning Session: 7:00 AM to 12:00 PM
Evening Session: 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM
parent_birla_mandir_faq_4_c1b16c:
Temple: Birla Mandir
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is there an entry fee or a digital ticket booking system?
Answer: No. Entry to the Birla Temple is completely free for all local and international tourists. There are no special paid darshan tickets or online booking protocols; visitors simply join the general walk-in queues.
parent_birla_mandir_faq_5_62a71e:
Temple: Birla Mandir
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Can I take photos or carry my mobile phone inside?
Answer: Strictly No. Photography, videography, and all electronic gadgets (including mobile phones, smartwatches, and cameras) are banned inside the complex. You must deposit your devices at the free security cloakroom booth near the entrance steps before heading up.
parent_birla_mandir_faq_6_066336:
Temple: Birla Mandir
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is the temple accessible for elderly individuals or disabled tourists?
Answer: Yes. While the path to the top of the hillock features steep marble staircases, the management operates an on-site elevator/lift facility specifically reserved for senior citizens and physically challenged individuals.
parent_birla_mandir_faq_7_f68a50:
Temple: Birla Mandir
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the peak crowd hours to avoid when planning a visit?
Answer: Weekdays (Monday to Thursday) are highly peaceful and uncrowded. However, weekends (Friday to Sunday) see massive crowd surges of local families and tourists. Waiting times in the queue lines spike significantly between 6:30 PM and 8:30 PM on Sundays.

parent_chilkur_festivals_complete:
Temple: Chilkur
Category: Festivals
File: festivals.json

Festival Name: Annual Brahmotsavams
Month: Chaitra Masam (usually March-April; varies annually according to the Hindu lunar calendar)
Importance: Brahmotsavams is one of the major annual festivals celebrated at Chilkur Balaji Temple. The festival includes special rituals, homas, decorations, and processions. Garuda Prasadam has historically been associated with the Brahmotsavam period, although temple management frequently updates its availability, distribution format, and schedule from year to year to ensure proper crowd management.
Description: The annual Brahmotsavam is generally conducted over seven days, starting with the preliminary Ankurarpanam ritual. Daily vehicle processions (Vahanams) are a key element of the week.

Schedule:
  - Opening: Ankurarpanam (Sacred seed sowing)
  - Day 1: Dwajarohanam (Garuda flag-hoisting ceremony)
  - Mid-festival: Kalyanotsavam (Celestial marriage) and special Vahana Sevas
  - Later: Rathotsavam (Chariot procession)
  - Later: Ashwavahanam (Horse-vehicle procession)
  - Final day: Chakrasnanam / Chakra Theertham followed by conclusion of the festival

---

Festival Name: Vaikunta Ekadasi
Month: Margashirsha / Dhanur Masam (varies annually according to the Hindu lunar calendar)
Importance: Vaikunta Ekadasi is an important Vaishnava observance celebrated at Chilkur Balaji Temple. Due to high pilgrim surges on this day, specific darshan protocols, access to designated pathways or gateways, and line waiting times can vary significantly by year.
Description: The date changes annually based on lunar cycles. Devotees are advised to verify special entry configurations and potential changes to pradakshina rules with temple administrators closer to the event date.

---

Festival Name: Poolangi
Month: Varies annually according to the Hindu lunar calendar
Importance: Poolangi is an important religious observance associated with Chilkur Balaji Temple. It is recognized by local government listings, including the Rangareddy District administration, as a key festive occasion that draws large crowds of visiting devotees.
Description: The observance centers around elaborate, special floral decorations (Alankaram) completely adorning the main deity.

---

Festival Name: Annakota
Month: Varies annually according to the Hindu lunar calendar
Importance: Annakota is another prominent religious observance celebrated at Chilkur Balaji Temple and is specifically cited by the Rangareddy District government as a major event in the temple's calendar.
Description: Features dedicated food offerings and traditional rituals. Devotees should verify the specific Gregorian date and timing with local temple handlers for the current year.

parent_chilkur_description_8a851fff:
Temple: Chilkur
Category: Description
File: temple.json

Description: Chilkur Balaji Temple, the Abode of Lord Venkateshwara – at Chilkur village of Rangareddy District in Telangana State is one of the ancient and famous Vaishnavite temples. The shrine deserves a special mention in terms of its simplicity and spiritual sanctity and is one of the oldest and most famous temples in Telangana State. Existence of this shrine is lost in the mists of antiquity and local traditions date the temple back half a millennium. The presiding Deity – Lord Balaji Venkateshwara in the form of a Swayambhu idol (accompanied by Sridevi and Bhoodevi) is known for his boundless benevolence in fulfilling the wishes of the devotees. This Shrine is popularly known as "Telangana Tirupati" and also famously as the "Visa Balaji Temple" because of the widespread belief that praying here helps devotees secure visas for foreign travel, especially for studies and employment. A unique feature of this temple is that it operates without government control, has no hundi (donation box), accepts no money or ornaments from devotees, and does not provide any VIP or paid fast-track darshan queues.
parent_chilkur_history_8d50330c:
Temple: Chilkur
Category: History
File: temple.json

History: History mentions that the temple was built during the time of Akkanna and Madanna, the uncles of Bhakta Ramdas (circa 17th century AD / 500 years ago). According to tradition, a devotee who used to visit Tirupati every year fell seriously ill and could not travel. Lord Venkateshwara appeared in his dream and said, "I am right here in the jungle nearby. You don't have to worry." The devotee at once moved to the place indicated by the Lord in the dream and saw a mole-hill there, which he dug up. Accidentally, the axe struck Lord Balaji's idol covered by the mole-hill below the chin and on the chest, and surprisingly blood started flowing profusely from the "wounds", flooding the ground and turning it scarlet. The devotee could not believe his eyes. He heard a voice from the air which said, "Flood the mole-hill with cow's milk." When the devotee did so, a Swayambhu idol of Lord Balaji accompanied by Sridevi and Bhoodevi was found, and this idol was installed with the due rites and a temple built for it.

Mythology: According to tradition, a devotee who used to visit Tirupati every year fell seriously ill and could not travel. Lord Venkateshwara appeared in his dream and said, "I am right here in the jungle nearby. You don't have to worry." The devotee at once moved to the place indicated by the Lord in the dream and saw a mole-hill there, which he dug up. Accidentally, the axe struck Lord Balaji's idol covered by the mole-hill below the chin and on the chest, and surprisingly blood started flowing profusely from the "wounds", flooding the ground and turning it scarlet. The devotee could not believe his eyes. He heard a voice from the air which said, "Flood the mole-hill with cow's milk." When the devotee did so, a Swayambhu idol of Lord Balaji accompanied by Sridevi and Bhoodevi was found, and this idol was installed with the due rites and a temple built for it. Historical & Spiritual Importance: With the earnest desire to revive the former glory and importance of the temple, the idol of Ammavaru was installed in 1963 (the year following the Chinese aggression). When the aggression was unilaterally vacated, Ammavaru was given the name of Rajya Lakshmi, signifying this welcome event. The unique feature of this idol is that lotus flowers are held in three hands and the fourth hand is in a position towards the lotus feet, which signifies the doctrine of Saranagathi (surrender).

parent_dharmapuri_wheelchair_accessibili:

Is Wheelchair Friendly: No

Details:
  - Walking Aids Recommended: Navigating the stone temple courtyards (Prakarams) and long flight of stone steps down to the Godavari riverbank can be physically demanding; walking sticks are advised.
  - Lightweight Folding Stool Recommended: Long queues during peak hours (1 to 2.5 hours on Saturdays/Tuesdays) or waiting times at the Godavari ghats can be tiring. Carrying a small lightweight folding stool is strongly recommended for senior citizens.
  - Thick Cotton Socks: Protects feet against intense afternoon heat radiation from the sun-baked stone temple courtyards while complying with ritual purity.
  - Medication Buffer: Pilgrims should carry a 2-day extra supply of BP, diabetes, or daily prescription medications, as specific brands may not be stocked locally in town.

parent_dharmapuri_safety_rules_9a0e6c59:
Temple: Dharmapuri
Category: Safety Rules
File: river_bank.json

Safety Rules: During monsoon surges, heavy upstream dam inflow causes rapid water rise and flood alerts, submerging lower steps. Heavy-duty security nets, anchored floating ropes, and bamboo barricades define safe boundaries. Stationed lifeguards on boats with lifebuoys and overhead multi-nozzle river water shower systems are deployed during peak events.
parent_dharmapuri_dress_code_1d09ca4d:
Temple: Dharmapuri
Category: Dress Code
File: rules.json

Men: Traditional attire like White Pancha, Dhoti, Kurta, or Pyjama. Standard formal shirts and trousers are allowed for general darshan, but traditional wear is mandatory for special sevas like Abhishekam and Kalyanotsavam.
Women: Saree with blouse, Chudidhar/Punjabi Dress with Dupatta, Half Saree, or Lehenga. Modern western clothing (shorts, sleeveless tops, ripped jeans) is strictly discouraged.
parent_dharmapuri_dos_26b0b0b8:
Temple: Dharmapuri
Category: Dos
File: rules.json

- Follow one-way pedestrian flow circuits from transit drop-offs to river and temple gates
- Bathe safely behind security nets, floating ropes, and bamboo barricades at river ghats or use overhead showers
- Maintain ritual purity (Madi) when staying at satralu/guest houses for family rituals
- Park private vehicles at peripheral parking lots along incoming highways during peak processing times
- Listen to public address announcements for safety instructions, missing persons, and queue wait times
parent_dharmapuri_donts_52858c42:
Temple: Dharmapuri
Category: Donts
File: rules.json

- Do not cross anchored floating ropes, security nets, or bamboo barricades into deep river water
- Do not drive motorized vehicles past the main Dharmapuri Temple Arch Kaman during processing peaks
- Do not perform Nithya Kalyanam or Nitya Nrusimha Homams during Bramhotsavalu period (27 Feb 2026 to 11 Mar 2026)
- No darshan for devotees on 3 March 2026 after 7:00 AM due to Lunar Eclipse temple closure
parent_dharmapuri_electronic_ban_5b2b36b:
Temple: Dharmapuri
Category: Electronic Ban
File: rules.json

Electronic Ban: Mobile phones, DSLRs, and cameras are strictly prohibited inside the Garbhagriha (inner sanctum). Photography and videography of the main deity are forbidden. While phones are tolerated in the outer courtyard, photography during main rituals/sevas is disallowed. Drones and tripods are strictly banned across the entire temple complex without official Devastanam permission. Locker facilities are available near the entrance to deposit devices.
parent_dharmapuri_safety_guidelines_2458:
Temple: Dharmapuri
Category: Safety Guidelines
File: rules.json

Safety Guidelines: During monsoon surge, stay clear of submerging lower steps on Godavari River Ghat. Stationed lifeguards on boats monitor bathing areas. Lost-and-found reports and missing child announcements are handled via central loudspeaker networks and Police Command Control Room near Temple Arch Kaman. Temporary medical tents and 24/7 CHC handle heat exhaustion and emergency medical care.

parent_dharmapuri_description_5bfa059a:
Temple: Dharmapuri
Category: Description
File: temple.json

Description: Dharmapuri Kshetram is a sacred land and living confluence of Sanatana Dharma, magnificent historical heritage, and artistic grandeur, nestled on the banks of the holy River Godavari flowing as 'Dakshina Vahini' (southward flow). It is revered as one of the nine sacred Narasimha abodes (Nava Narasimha Kshetram) in India and serves as a powerful Hari-Hara Kshetram symbolizing spiritual unity between Shaivite and Vaishnavite traditions.
parent_dharmapuri_history_462c38b4:
Temple: Dharmapuri
Category: History
File: temple.json

History: The temple heritage endures from the era of King Dharmavarma of Vidarbha to the present day as a unique stream preserving Vedic knowledge and fine arts. The Kshetram has been patronised over a millennium by prominent dynasties including the Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas, and the Recharla Velama chiefs. It has also been enriched by literary luminaries like Sheshappa Kavi and Pingali Surana.
parent_dharmapuri_mythology_fbe6b76e:
Temple: Dharmapuri
Category: Mythology
File: temple.json

Mythology: Dharmapuri finds explicit mention in several sacred Puranas including the Skandha Purana and Brahmanda Purana. It is celebrated as a primary center for devotion and spiritual liberation since Puranic times. Lord Ramalingeshwara Swamy deity was installed by Lord Rama. A unique physical synthesis exists at the Satyavati temple where Lord Narasimha is placed directly on top of a Shiva Panamattam.

parent_edupayal_festivals_complete:
Temple: Edupayal
Category: Festivals
File: festivals.json

Festival Name: Bramhotsavalu (Jatara) 2026
Description: The annual Edupayala Jatara is a major and notified festival in Medak district, celebrated with massive grandeur at the confluence of the seven streams of the Manjeera River. In 2026, the 3-day annual festival was celebrated during Maha Shivaratri (15 February to 17 February 2026). Millions of pilgrims from Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Maharashtra participated.
Programme Schedule
15 Feb 2026 (Maha Shivaratri): Special Abhishekams, Kumkumarchana, continuous darshan, and commencement of the annual Jatara.
16 Feb 2026: Devotees take holy dips at the confluence of the seven streams. Traditional cultural activities and Bandi Utsavam (decorated bullock cart procession) are conducted during the festival.
17 Feb 2026: Rathotsavam (chariot procession) and concluding religious ceremonies of the annual Jatara.
During the annual Jatara, the temple extends darshan hours and makes special arrangements to accommodate the large influx of devotees.
Month: Maha Shivaratri (15 February to 17 February 2026)
Importance: Major and notified festival in Medak district, celebrated with massive grandeur at the confluence of the seven streams of the Manjeera River.

---

Festival Name: Ashada Bonalu & Folk Traditions
Description: During the month of Ashada (July/August), the temple becomes vibrant with local folk performances:
Oggu Kathalu & Folk Music: Traditional storytellers perform native folk stories detailing the legends of Goddess Durga.
Pothuraju Dances: Traditional dances performed during Bonalu, where participants whip themselves to chase away evil spirits.
Month: Ashada (July/August)
Importance: The Edupayala temple plays a central role in preserving the rural cultural arts of Telangana.

---

Festival Name: Bathukamma Panduga
Description: During Dussehra, local women gather at the riverbanks to float colorful flower stacks (Bathukammas) in the seven streams of the river.
Month: Dussehra
Importance: Local women gather at the riverbanks to float colorful flower stacks (Bathukammas) in the seven streams of the river.

---

Festival Name: Ashada Masotsavams 2026
Description: Ashada Masam is a highly sacred period at the Edupayala temple, celebrating the maternal and protective aspects of Goddess Durga.
Festival Dates & Details
Start Date: 15 July 2026 (Wednesday)
End Date: 12 August 2026 (Wednesday)
Auspicious Days: Every Sunday and Friday during this month sees a massive influx of local pilgrims.
Core Rituals & Spiritual Significance
Bonam Offerings: Devotees prepare cooked rice with jaggery and milk in decorated pots, offering them to the Goddess in gratitude for family well-being.
Chandi Homam: Performed every Friday to invoke the protective energies of the deity.
River Snanam: Pilgrims take a purification bath in the flowing Manjeera streams before entering the cave shrine.
Month: 15 July 2026 (Wednesday) to 12 August 2026 (Wednesday)
Importance: Ashada Masam is a highly sacred period at the Edupayala temple, celebrating the maternal and protective aspects of Goddess Durga.

parent_edupayal_description_5a01d52e:
Temple: Edupayal
Category: Description
File: temple.json

Description: Situated in Nagasanpally village of Papannapet Mandal in Medak District, the sacred shrine of Sri Edupayala Vana Durga Bhavani Devalayam is one of the most powerful Shakti shrines in Telangana. Nestled in a forest area at the confluence of seven streams of the Manjeera River, the temple's location combines natural beauty with deep spiritual energy.

Swayambhu Vana Durga Bhavani: The deity, Vana Durga Bhavani, is Swayambhu (self-manifested) in the form of a natural stone structure located in the middle of the riverbed. The stone is adorned with turmeric and kumkum by the priests. During monsoons, the rising Manjeera River flows directly over the feet of the Goddess (known as Charan Sparsh or Jala Abhishekam by nature).

Confluence of Seven Streams (Edu Payalu): The name "Edupayala" translates to "seven streams" (Edu = seven, Payalu = streams) of the Manjeera River. According to the Bhavishyothara Purana, Maharaja Janamejaya (the son of Parikshit, grandson of Arjuna) performed a Sarpa Yagna at this location to rid himself of the curse of snake-bite. The seven streams were formed to wash away the ashes and purify the site of the sacrifice.

Historical & Cultural Importance: Dating back to the 12th century, the temple is heavily integrated with the rural culture of Telangana. It serves as a central hub during the monsoon and Ashada months, where thousands of women carry decorated pots of cooked rice, jaggery, and neem leaves (Bonalu) on their heads to offer to the Goddess.

Description: Sri Jogulamba Devi Temple is located at Alampur in Jogulamba Gadwal district of Telangana. It is one of the eighteen revered Maha Shakti Peethas in India (5th of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas) and is dedicated to Goddess Jogulamba, a fierce form of Goddess Shakti. The temple is situated near the sacred confluence of the Tungabhadra and Krishna rivers and is one of the most important pilgrimage destinations in South India. Goddess Jogulamba is worshipped in a fierce form and is believed to bless devotees with spiritual strength, protection and prosperity. The temple is also closely associated with the historic Nava Brahma Temples, making Alampur an important centre of both Shaivism and Shakti worship. Maintained by Endowments Department, Government of Telangana (Sri Jogulamba Devasthanam Board).
parent_jogulamba(new)_history_1230b5e7:
Temple: Jogulamba(New)
Category: History
File: temple.json

History: Alampur is an ancient temple town situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra River and is regarded as the western gateway to Srisailam. The Jogulamba Temple is closely associated with the Badami Chalukyas, who built the renowned Nava Brahma Temples during the 7th century CE. The region later came under the rule of several South Indian dynasties, which contributed to its religious and architectural importance. According to local tradition, the saint Rasa Siddha, who was closely associated with King Pulakesi II, played an important role in the construction of the Nava Brahma Temples. The original Jogulamba Temple was destroyed during the Bahmani invasions, and the idol of Goddess Jogulamba, along with the idols of Chandi and Mundi, was shifted to the Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple for protection. The idols remained there until 2005, when a new temple was reconstructed near the historic Nava Brahma Temple complex and the original idol of Goddess Jogulamba was reinstalled. Today, the temple remains one of the most sacred centres of Shakti worship in India.
parent_jogulamba(new)_mythology_9049ea8f:
Temple: Jogulamba(New)
Category: Mythology
File: temple.json

Mythology: Goddess Jogulamba is revered as the 5th of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas in India. Goddess Jogulamba is depicted in a powerful and fierce form sitting on a corpse. The animals on her head—a lizard, scorpion, and frog (and bat)—symbolize evil elements and signs of house degeneration. The Goddess destroys these forces to protect her devotees, which is why she is also called Gruha Chandi (Protector of Homes).

parent_kaleshvaram_faq_0_a9284a:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Who are the presiding deities at Kaleshwaram Temple?
Answer: Lord Kaleshwara (Lord Yama) and Lord Mukteshwara (Lord Shiva) are the presiding deities, enshrined together on a single pedestal (Panavattam).
parent_kaleshvaram_faq_1_e9b610:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What is unique about the Mukteshwara Shiva Linga?
Answer: The Mukteshwara Linga features two distinct holes/nostrils (Nasarandhras). Abhishekam water poured into these openings flows into subterranean channels connected to the holy river confluence.
parent_kaleshvaram_faq_2_dd56aa:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: In what order should a devotee worship at Kaleshwaram?
Answer: According to ancient temple tradition, devotees must worship Lord Kaleshwara (Yama) first before offering prayers to Lord Mukteshwara (Shiva).
parent_kaleshvaram_faq_3_add5f4:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What is Triveni Sangam at Kaleshwaram?
Answer: Triveni Sangam is the sacred confluence of three rivers at Kaleshwaram: River Godavari, River Pranahita, and the invisible subterranean River Saraswati.
parent_kaleshvaram_faq_4_e7bf5f:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Are online seva bookings available for Kaleshwaram Temple?
Answer: No. There is currently no authorized online booking system for Kaleshwaram Temple. All seva, abhishekam, and darshan tickets must be purchased in person at the temple counters.
parent_kaleshvaram_faq_5_7695d0:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the temple operating hours?
Answer: The temple is open daily from 4:30 AM to 1:00 PM and reopens from 3:30 PM to 8:00 PM. It remains closed during the afternoon break between 1:00 PM and 3:30 PM.
parent_kaleshvaram_faq_6_fd856d:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Which are the main sub-temples in the complex?
Answer: Key sub-shrines include Sri Subhananda Devi (Goddess Parvati) Temple, Sri Maha Saraswati Temple, Sri Suryanarayana Temple, Sri Adi Mukteshwara Temple, and Sri Dattatreya Temple.
parent_kaleshvaram_faq_7_da238d:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: How can I reach Kaleshwaram Temple?
Answer: Kaleshwaram is reachable by RTC buses via Manthani and Bhupalpally. The nearest major railway stations are Ramagundam (~65 km), Peddapalli (~75 km), and Mancherial (~70 km).

Festival Name: Mahasivarathri Jathra
Description: Mahasivarathri Jathra is the grandest annual festival celebrated at Kaleshwaram. Hundreds of thousands of pilgrims gather at the shrine. The temple remains open round-the-clock during the festival. Elaborate arrangements, special queue lines, and cultural programs are organized by the District Administration and Endowments Department.
Month: February or March
Importance: Grandest annual festival, attracting pilgrims from Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh.

---

Festival Name: Karthika Masotsavam & Karthika Purnima
Description: The entire month of Karthika is celebrated with high fervor. Thousands of devotees perform holy dips in the Triveni Sangam, participate in Deepotsavam (lighting of oil lamps along the river banks and temple complex), and offer Laksha Bilwapatri Archana and Abhishekams.
Month: Karthika (October/November)
Importance: Holy month dedicated to Lord Shiva, marked by holy river baths, lamp lighting, and special archana.

---

Festival Name: Other Festivals
Description: Other major festivals celebrated include Sri Rama Navami, Ganesh Navarathrotsavams, Devi Navarathrotsavams (Dussehra), Shravana Masam rituals, Hanuman Jayanthi, Vasantha Navaratri, and Pranahita & Godavari Pushkaralu (every 12 years).
Month: Various
Importance: Annual celebrations and periodic river festivals.

parent_kaleshvaram_significance_61f557c9:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Significance
File: river_bank.json

Significance: The temple is situated on the sacred banks of the Dakshina Triveni Sangamam — the holy confluence of three rivers: River Godavari, River Pranahita, and the invisible subterranean River Saraswati (Antarvahini). Devotees traditionally take a holy dip (Sangama Snanam) at the Triveni Sangam bathing ghats before entering the temple complex for darshan. The river bank is famous for Godavari Pushkaralu and Pranahita Pushkaralu (holy river festivals held once every 12 years), attracting millions of pilgrims across India.
parent_kaleshvaram_dress_code_11e4f856:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Dress Code
File: rules.json

Men: Any decent traditional outfit for Darshan. For Garbhagriha Abhishekam, men must remove Shirt and Vest (Dhoti / Pancha required).
Women: Any decent traditional outfit for Darshan. For Garbhagriha Abhishekam, women must wear Saree or Chudidhar with Dupatta.
parent_kaleshvaram_dos_e6f3f0ff:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Dos
File: rules.json

- Do take a holy bath in the Triveni Sangam (Godavari, Pranahita, Saraswati river confluence) before entering the temple queue lines.
- Do offer prayers to Lord Kaleshwara (Yama) FIRST, before worshipping Lord Mukteshwara (Shiva) as per ancient temple tradition.
- Do maintain quiet and follow line discipline during peak rush hours.
- Do deposit footwear, leather items, and electronic gadgets at designated cloakrooms outside.
- Do wear traditional attire and place tilak/kumkum on your forehead as a mark of devotion.
parent_kaleshvaram_donts_29b82133:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Donts
File: rules.json

- Don't wear any footwear inside or around the main temple boundary walls.
- Don't take photographs or record videos inside the sanctum sanctorum (Garbhagriha); cameras and cell phones are strictly prohibited.
- Don't consume non-vegetarian food, alcohol, or tobacco products before or during your temple visit.
- Don't carry plastic bags, matchboxes, or sharp objects inside security check zones.
- Don't deal with unauthorized brokers or touts promising quick darshan.

parent_kaleshvaram_description_1c72c849:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Description
File: temple.json

Description: Abode of Lord Kaleshwara & Lord Mukteshwara – at Kaleshwaram village is one of the most ancient, revered, and architecturally unique Shaivite shrines in South India. The presiding deity is unique because two Shiva Lingas—Lord Kaleshwara and Lord Mukteshwara—are enshrined together on a single pedestal (Panavattam). Another divine wonder is the presence of two distinct nostrils (Nasarandhras) on the Mukteshwara Linga. Water poured during Abhishekam into these openings flows through subterranean channels and drains directly into the holy Triveni Sangam river bed. Devotees must first worship Lord Kaleshwara before proceeding to Lord Mukteshwara.
parent_kaleshvaram_history_84859b08:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: History
File: temple.json

History: Skanda Purana mentions that Lord Yama Dharma Raja performed severe penance at this spot after discovering that devotees worshipping Lord Shiva here were directly attaining salvation, leaving Yama's realm (Yama Loka) empty. Pleased with his penance, Lord Shiva granted Yama a spot alongside Him on the same pedestal and ordained that Yama (Kaleshwara) be worshipped first.

Kaleshwaram is also revered as one of the cornerstone shrines of Telugu heritage under the 'Trilinga Desam' connection, bounded by three famous shrines: Srisailam (Andhra Pradesh), Draksharamam (Andhra Pradesh), and Kaleshwaram (Telangana).
parent_kaleshvaram_mythology_ff98fe91:
Temple: Kaleshvaram
Category: Mythology
File: temple.json

Mythology: Lord Shiva granted Yama a spot alongside Him on the same pedestal. Devotees worship Lord Yama first to destroy fear of death and grant ultimate liberation (Moksha). Worshipping the twin Lingas together is a unique spiritual custom.

parent_karmanghat_faq_0_a243b1:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Who is the presiding deity of the temple?
Answer: Lord Hanuman (Dhyana Anjaneya, depicting Hanuman in a meditative posture) is the presiding deity of the temple.
parent_karmanghat_faq_1_7ed0b4:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the regular temple timings?
Answer: On regular days (Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sun), the temple is open from 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 4:30 PM to 8:30 PM. On Tuesdays and Saturdays, extended hours apply: 5:30 AM to 1:00 PM and 4:30 PM to 9:00 PM.
parent_karmanghat_faq_2_b58730:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Are online sevas and puja bookings available?
Answer: Yes. Devotees can book various sevas, vehicle pujas, and special darshan tickets online via the official Telangana Temple Endowments portal (karmanghattemple.telangana.gov.in).
parent_karmanghat_faq_3_50ab0c:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is Annadanam (free food) available at the temple?
Answer: Yes. The temple management conducts Annadanam (free meal distribution) on a daily basis for visiting devotees.
parent_karmanghat_faq_4_c680b5:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Can devotees make online donations?
Answer: Yes. Online donations for general temple maintenance, Nitya Annadanam, and specific sevas can be made through the Telangana Endowments booking portal.
parent_karmanghat_faq_5_39c84c:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Which major festivals are celebrated here?
Answer: Hanuman Jayanti and Sri Rama Navami are celebrated grandly, along with Ugadi, Dussehra, and Kartika Masam.
parent_karmanghat_faq_6_e5fc6d:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: How can I reach Sri Karmanghat Hanuman Temple?
Answer: The temple is located at Karmanghat on the Inner Ring Road near Champapet, Hyderabad. It is easily accessible via TSRTC buses, autos, or by metro (LB Nagar Metro Station is ~2 km away).
parent_karmanghat_faq_7_72c49c:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is parking available at the temple premises?
Answer: Yes. Parking space is available near the outer entrance complex for two-wheelers and four-wheelers.
parent_karmanghat_faq_8_de5d30:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is photography allowed inside the temple?
Answer: Photography and mobile phone usage are strictly prohibited inside the inner sanctum (Garbhagriha). Photos are only allowed in outer courtyard zones where permitted.
parent_karmanghat_faq_9_25cebc:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Why is the Karmanghat Hanuman Temple famous?
Answer: Built around 1198 AD by Kakatiya ruler Prola II, it is one of the oldest and most historical temples in Hyderabad, legendary for withstanding Aurangzeb's siege on the city.
parent_karmanghat_festivals_complete:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Festivals
File: festivals.json

Festival Name: Hanuman Jayanti
Description: The birth anniversary of Lord Hanuman, the presiding deity of the temple. It is the most significant and grandly celebrated festival here, drawing over a hundred thousand devotees. The temple remains open for extended hours, featuring special Abhishekams, betel leaf garlands (Aku Puja), devotional singing, and continuous Annadanam. The temple is a key focal point for the Hanuman Jayanti Shobha Yatra in Hyderabad.
Month: Chaitra (March/April) / Vaishakha
Importance: Major & grandest annual festival

---

Festival Name: Sri Rama Navami
Description: Marks the birth anniversary of Lord Rama. Given Lord Hanuman's deep devotion to Lord Rama, Sri Rama Navami is celebrated with great religious fervor, including special Akhanda Rama Nama chanting and the divine Sita Rama Kalyanotsavam.
Month: Chaitra (March/April)
Importance: Major annual festival

---

Festival Name: Maha Shivaratri
Description: Celebrated grandly at the within-complex shrine of Lord Shiva with night-long Pujas, Abhishekam, and special devotional programs.
Month: Phalguna / Magha (February/March)
Importance: Significant temple festival

---

Festival Name: Ugadi & Kartika Masam
Description: Telugu New Year (Ugadi) involves Panchanga Sravanam at the temple. During Kartika Masam, special Deepotsavam (lighting of lamps) takes place throughout the courtyard.
Month: Chaitra (March) & Kartika (October/November)
Importance: Seasonal cultural & spiritual celebrations

parent_karmanghat_dress_code_294dbfc6:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Dress Code
File: rules.json

Men: Recommended: Formal or traditional attire including a Dhoti, Kurta-Pyjama, or neat formal shirts paired with regular trousers / full pants. Strictly Banned: T-shirts containing explicit graphics/slogans, shorts, three-fourths, ripped jeans, or gym track pants.
Women: Recommended: Traditional Indian attire such as a Saree, Half-Saree, or Salwar Kameez / Chudidhar paired with a dupatta or upper cloth. Strictly Banned: Shorts, mini-skirts, low-waist jeans, sleeveless tops, tank tops, or crop tops that expose the legs, shoulders, or arms.
parent_karmanghat_dos_48f7e800:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Dos
File: rules.json

- Do keep your mind fresh and leave all your negative, stress and pain behind.
- Do open your eyes while having Darshan.
- Do observe maintain silence inside the Temple.
- Do respect ancient customs and usages while in temple premises.
- Do respect and promote religious sentiments among co-pilgrims.
- Do deposit your offerings & Kanukas in the Hundi Only.
- Do keep the temple premises Clean & Hygienic.
- Do contact Information centre for unknown information about devasthanam.
- Do watch your valuables very carefully (i.e Wallets, Gold Ornaments, Luggage bags etc.,) as there is fear of theft.
parent_karmanghat_donts_e5b21b63:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Donts
File: rules.json

- Don't carry Jewellery and Cash in excess with you.
- Don't wear footwear in and around the premises of the Temple.
- Don't approach brokers for quick Darshan.
- Don't throw away the Prasadam and teertham given to you at the temple.
- Don't carry any weapon inside the temple.
- Don't eat non-vegetarian food.
- Don't consume liquor or other intoxicants.
- Don't smoke in and around temple premises.
- Don't wear any head guards like helmets, caps, turbans and hats inside the temple premises.
- Don't buy fake Prasadams from street vendors.
- Don't commit any act of violence or harshness, anger, Jealous in the temple premises.
- Don't quarrel in the temple premises.
- Don't rush in for Darshan but take your chance in the queue.
- Don't encourage beggary in and around temple premises.
- Don't split or be a nuisance inside the temple premises.
- Don't carry luggage bags and other belongs inside temple premises.

parent_karmanghat_description_a9c68a19:
Temple: Karmanghat
Category: Description
File: temple.json

Description: The Karmanghat Hanuman Temple is one of the oldest and popular Hindu temples in Hyderabad, in the state of Telangana, India. The presiding deity of the temple is Lord Hanuman and the temple complex also houses other deities viz. Lord Rama, Lord Shiva, Goddess Saraswathi, Goddess Durga, Goddess Santoshimata, Lord Venugopala Swamy, and Lord Jagannath. The temple is located at Karmanghat, near Santoshnagar and closer to the Nagarjuna Sagar Ring Road. It was built in the 12th century A.D (approximately 1143). When a Kakatiya king went hunting and was resting under a tree, he heard the chanting of Lord Rama's name. Wondering who it was in the middle of a dense forest, he discovered a stone idol of Lord Hanuman, in seated posture and the voice coming from the vigraha. Having paid his respects, he returned to his capital, and that night, Lord appeared in his dream and asked him to construct a temple. The temple was built immediately and successive kings ruled it well. About 400 years later, Aurangzeb sent out his armies to all corners of the country for further expansion of Mughal Empire. At this temple, the army couldn't even step close to the compound wall. When the general reported this to Aurangzeb, he himself went with a crow bar to break down the temple. At the threshold of the temple, he heard a deafening roar rumbling like thunder, and the crowbar slipped from his hands as he was shaking in fear. Then he heard a voice in the heavens "Mandir todna hai rajan, to kar man ghat" (translation: "If you want to break down the temple, O King, harden your heart.") which is why the place got the name kar-man-ghat. And to this day, Lord Anjaneya sits peacefully meditating and blessing devotees, as Dhyana Anjaneya Swamy.

parent_medaram_festivals_complete:
Temple: Medaram
Category: Festivals
File: festivals.json

Festival Name: Medaram Sammakka-Saralamma Maha Jathara (Biennial 4-Day Mega Festival)
Month: Magha Masam full moon (Magha Sudha Purnima - Late January / February)
Importance: Asia’s largest tribal congregation and the second-largest religious gathering in India after the Kumbh Mela. Officially declared a State Festival by the Government of Telangana in 1998.
Description: Celebrated once every two years (biennially) during the full moon of Magha Masam. Over 1.5 to 1.75 crore (15–17.5 million) pilgrims gather over four days in Medaram forest village. Devotees honor the supreme sacrifice of the Koya tribal mother and daughter who fought against Kakatiya dynasty taxation and oppression.

Schedule:
    Date: Day 1 (Wednesday)
    Tithi Event: Arrival of Saralamma, Pagididda Raju, and Govinda Raju
    Details: Secret morning pujas conducted by Koya priests. In the evening, Goddess Saralamma's deity form is brought from Kannepally village shrine via Jampanna Vagu to the Medaram Gaddelu platform. Simultaneously, Pagididda Raju is brought from Punugondla village and Govinda Raju from Kondayi village amidst traditional Koya music, Aarti, and tribal processions.
---
    Date: Day 2 (Thursday)
    Tithi Event: Arrival of Goddess Sammakka (Edurukolla Ghattam)
    Details: Arrival of Goddess Sammakka from Chilakala Gutta hill onto the main Gadde platform. Koya tribal priests bring the divine Kumkuma Bharanam (casket of vermilion) amidst intense spiritual fervor. District Superintendent of Police (SP) fires three gunshots into the air as official state homage to mark her arrival.
---
    Date: Day 3 (Friday)
    Tithi Event: Peak Day / Maha Darshanam & Offering of Mokkubadulu & Bangaram
    Details: The peak day of the Jathara when both deities reside on the Gaddelu platform. Crores of devotees take Punya Snanams (holy dips) in Jampanna Vagu, offer 'Odi Biyyam' (sacred rice mix), 'Saare', and present 'Bangaram' (Jaggery equal to or exceeding their body weight) as fulfillment of vows.
---
    Date: Day 4 (Saturday)
    Tithi Event: Vana Pravesham (Return to the Forest)
    Details: The concluding day of the 4-day festival. After afternoon pujas and rituals, state security honors are accorded again as the deities symbolically return to their sacred forest abodes until the next biennial Jathara.
---

---

Festival Name: Mini Jathara (Manda Melige / Annual Observance)
Month: Magha Masam (February - Non-Jathara Years)
Importance: Annual tribal ritual observance and shrine maintenance at Medaram
Description: Conducted in non-Maha Jathara years by hereditary Koya priests (Siddaboina and Kene family clans). A 4-day ritual called 'Manda Melige' is performed at Medaram, Kannepally, Punugondla, and Kondayi shrines to clean the altars, perform sacred forest offerings, and preserve Koya spiritual traditions.

Schedule:
    Date: Day 1 (Wednesday)
    Tithi Event: Manda Melige & Temple Cleaning
    Details: Koya priests perform sacred cleaning and purification rituals at the Medaram Gaddelu and Kannepally shrines.
---
    Date: Day 2 (Thursday)
    Tithi Event: Forest Offerings & Alankarams
    Details: Special private pujas and traditional forest offerings are conducted under tree covers by the tribal clan leaders.
---
    Date: Day 3 (Friday)
    Tithi Event: Public Darshan & Local Devotee Offerings
    Details: Devotees from nearby forest districts visit for quiet darshan and offer jaggery and coconuts without the massive multi-million crowds.
---
    Date: Day 4 (Saturday)
    Tithi Event: Conclusion of Manda Melige
    Details: Final prayers and sealing of sacred items until the next observance.
---

Significance: Jampanna Vagu is a sacred forest stream (tributary of Sampenga Vagu/Godavari River) named after Jampanna, the tribal warrior prince and son of Goddess Sammakka. He fought valiantly against Kakatiya forces and laid down his life in this stream. Tribal tradition attributes the stream's natural reddish tint to Jampanna's blood (geologically rich in red soil nutrients). Devotees perform Punya Snanams (holy dips) here to wash away sins, seek healing, and pay homage to tribal martyrs before offering prayers at the Gaddelu platform.

parent_medaram_description_88f2aa5b:
Temple: Medaram
Category: Description
File: temple.json

Description: Abode of Tribal Goddesses Sammakka & Saralamma – located at Medaram Village of SS Tadvai Mandal in Mulugu District (formerly Warangal/Jayashankar Bhupalpally district), Telangana State. Medaram Sammakka Saralamma Maha Jathara is Asia’s largest tribal congregation and the second-largest religious gathering in India after the Kumbha Mela. The festival was officially declared a State Festival by the Government of Telangana in 1998.

Presiding Deities:
The presiding deities of Medaram are the revered mother-daughter duo, Goddess Sammakka and Goddess Saralamma, worshipped along with Pagididda Raju (husband of Sammakka) and Govinda Raju (husband of Saralamma). Unlike traditional Vedic temples, there are no stone idols or brick structures in the main sanctum. Instead, the deities are represented on elevated wooden platforms known as "Gaddelu" amidst the dense forest environment.
parent_medaram_history_d15b5a1a:
Temple: Medaram
Category: History
File: temple.json

History: The Battle against Injustice (13th Century AD): During the 13th century AD, Medaram was a tribal region ruled by Pagididda Raju, a feudatory chief under Kakatiya King Prataparudra of Warangal. Due to severe drought, Pagididda Raju was unable to pay tribute tax to the Kakatiya empire. The Kakatiya forces invaded the tribal belt.

The Martyrdom: Pagididda Raju, his daughter Saralamma, son Jampanna, and son-in-law Govinda Raju fought heroically against the massive Kakatiya army and sacrificed their lives. Sammakka fought fiercely, inflicting heavy damage on the army. Upon being fatally wounded, she walked towards Chilakala Gutta (a nearby hill) and disappeared into the forest, leaving behind a container of vermilion (Casket of Kumkuma / Nawa Bharanam).
parent_medaram_mythology_d86756d9:
Temple: Medaram
Category: Mythology
File: temple.json

Mythology: Divine Manifestation: The Koya tribal hunters who pursued Sammakka found a glowing box of Kumkuma surrounded by tigers and peacocks. They recognized her divine power and started worshipping her as an incarnation of Adi Parashakti who protects her devotees from distress. Devotees honor the supreme sacrifice of the mother and daughter who fought against tyranny and unjust taxation. The festival represents pure indigenous tribal heritage (Koya tradition) performed strictly by traditional Koya Pujaris (priests). It has no Vedic or Brahminical rituals.

Temple: Ramappa
Category: Wheelchair Accessibility
File: elderly_ppl.json

Is Wheelchair Friendly: No

Details:
  - Not Wheelchair Friendly: The temple is built on a high, star-shaped raised platform typical of Kakatiya architecture. There are no ramps leading up to this platform. [[1](https://tourism.telangana.gov.in/destinations/ramappa#:~:text=The%20temple%20is%20built%20on,platform%2C%20with%20intricate%20carvings%20depicting)]
  - Physical Stairs Required: Visitors must physically climb a flight of steep stone steps to access the main deck and view the inner sanctum. Dependent wheelchair users cannot access the upper structure smoothly.
  - Flat Ground Premises: The surrounding outer lawn and archaeological pathways maintained by the ASI are relatively flat and can accommodate manual wheelchairs, but the actual temple structure is not accessible without climbing steps.

parent_ramappa_faq_0_492e23:
Temple: Ramappa
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Why is the Ramappa Temple famous globally?
Answer: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed in 2021) renowned for its 13th-century Kakatiya architecture. It is celebrated for its intricate black basalt carvings, a beautifully polished Nandi statue, and the engineering marvel of its light, "floating bricks" used in the roof construction.
parent_ramappa_faq_1_3fdf23:
Temple: Ramappa
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Who built the Ramappa Temple and when?
Answer: The temple was constructed in 1213 AD during the reign of the Kakatiya King Ganapati Deva. It was commissioned by his brilliant military general, Recharla Rudra.
parent_ramappa_faq_2_1a1298:
Temple: Ramappa
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Why is it named "Ramappa" if it is dedicated to Lord Shiva?
Answer: This is perhaps the only temple in India named after its chief sculptor/architect, Ramappa, rather than the presiding deity. The main deity worshipped inside the inner sanctum is technically called Ramalingeshwara Swamy (Lord Shiva).
parent_ramappa_faq_3_210b77:
Temple: Ramappa
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the opening hours and entry ticket prices?
Answer: The temple complex is open daily from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM. The official ASI entry fees are:
Indian Citizens: ₹25 per person.
Foreign Tourists: ₹300 per person.
Children (Below 15 years): Free entry.
parent_ramappa_faq_4_9813d9:
Temple: Ramappa
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Is there a specific dress code required for visitors?
Answer: While there is no rigid traditional dress code enforced by the ASI, it is an active place of worship. Visitors are strongly advised to dress modestly. Avoid shorts, sleeveless tops, or short skirts out of respect for local customs.
parent_ramappa_faq_5_f819fd:
Temple: Ramappa
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Are there certified tour guides available at the location?
Answer: Yes. Certified ASI guides are available near the ticketing counter. Hiring them is highly recommended (usually costing around ₹200–₹300). They will walk you through the history of the carvings and demonstrate how the special lightweight bricks float on water.
parent_ramappa_faq_6_0c0541:

parent_ramappa_history_92b9023d:
Temple: Ramappa
Category: History
File: temple.json

History: Built in 1213 CE by Racherla Rudra, a general under the Kakatiya ruler King Ganapati Deva. Popularly named after its master sculptor or architect, Ramappa, making it one of the rare Indian temples named after its artisan rather than its presiding deity. Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2021.
parent_ramappa_mythology_4b308d9b:
Temple: Ramappa
Category: Mythology
File: temple.json

Mythology: Features 13th-century Kakatiya architecture incorporating floating bricks technology (roof shikhara constructed using lightweight porous bricks that float on water) and sandbox foundation technique for earthquake resistance. Dolerite/basalt stone pillars feature mirror-polished carved dancer (Madanika) figures.

Question: What is the significance of Srisaila Mahakshetram?
Answer: Srisaila Mahakshetram is considered Kailasa on Earth. It is the only temple where the 2nd Jyotirlinga (Mallikarjuna Swamy) and the 6th Maha Shakti Peetha (Bhramaramba Devi) exist together under one temple premise.
parent_srisaila_faq_1_d97c01:
Temple: Srisaila
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the alternate names of Srisailam mentioned in ancient texts?
Answer: Srisailam is known by names such as Srigiri, Sirigiri, Sriparvatam, Srinagam, Kailasa on Earth, Bhuvi Kailasam, Southern Kashi, Chakora Shetagiri, Prasunachala, and Sirimala.
parent_srisaila_faq_2_739ad8:
Temple: Srisaila
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the four main gateways (Dwaralu) of Srisailam?
Answer: The four main entrances are Tripuranthakam (Eastern Gateway), Alampuram (Western Gateway), Umamaheshwaram (Northern Gateway), and Siddhavatam (Southern Gateway).
parent_srisaila_faq_3_221e84:
Temple: Srisaila
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What are the four sub-gateways (Upa Dwaralu) of Srisailam?
Answer: The four sub-gateways are Skandasomeshwaram / Somasila (South-East), Pushpagiri (South-West), Sangameshwaram (Confluence of 7 rivers), and Eleshwaram.
parent_srisaila_faq_4_3839a4:
Temple: Srisaila
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Why is Lord Shiva called Mallikarjuna at Srisailam?
Answer: Lord Shiva entered an Arjuna tree entwined by a Jasmine (Mallika) creeper. Furthermore, Princess Chandravathi offered a pure, never-withering garland of jasmine (Mallika) flowers to Lord Shiva, which he tied around his head.
parent_srisaila_faq_5_a4b71a:
Temple: Srisaila
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Who established the five Lingams (Pancha Lingalu) in the temple courtyard?
Answer: The five Pandava brothers—Yudhishtara, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva—established the five Lingams under their respective names during their visit.
parent_srisaila_faq_6_1b4ff3:
Temple: Srisaila
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: Why did Lord Rama establish Sahasralingam at Srisailam?
Answer: After slaying Ravana, Lord Rama was consumed by Brahmahatyadosham. Following Agastya Maharshi's advice, Lord Rama along with Sita Devi and Lakshmana visited Srisailam and established Sahasralingam to cleanse the burden.
parent_srisaila_faq_7_c5600e:
Temple: Srisaila
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What is the significance of Sanagala Basavanna (Nandi)?
Answer: Nandi is the head of all Ganas and vehicle of Lord Shiva representing Dharma. Worshippers must seek consent from Nandi before worshipping Lord Shiva, as divinity comes through Dharma.
parent_srisaila_faq_8_4c58dc:
Temple: Srisaila
Category: Faq
File: faq.json

Question: What is Chintamani Ganapathi (Ratnagarbha Ganapathi)?
Answer: It is an exclusive form of Ganapathi at Srisailam, Shringeri, and Arunachalam. Brought by Lord Shiva and Parvathi, Chintamani Ganapathi eliminates the troubles of devotees.
parent_srisaila_faq_9_534893:
Temple: Srisaila
